notes: Overview: Mid-market SaaS (B2B product analytics) evaluating Redwood as replacement for current LLM vendor. Primary motivation: predictable economics + VPC/dedicated options for customer data residency.
Current stack: production chat + summarization + embeddings powered by vendor X (usage heavy during weekdays). Want drop-in migration with minimal UX regressions.

POC ask: run Hosted API POC using Redwood's openai-compat layer for 2 weeks. Team will execute 3 workloads: chat assistant (multi-turn), doc-search embeddings (10M doc corpus sample), reranking for recommendations.

Success criteria (engineering): p99 latency for 64-token responses <= 350ms (US-West), throughput 120 reqs/s steady, embedding cosine similarity delta <= 0.02 vs baseline for top-10 retrieval, no >5% drop in end-to-end conversion on chat flows in A/B test.
Success criteria (business): token cost delta vs current vendor <= -20% or equivalent SLA uplift; committed Dedicated pricing must show 30-40% unit cost improvement for 12mo commit.

Compatibility notes: team uses OpenAI-style prompts, function-calling, and streaming. Concern: tokenization differences change prompt token counts and stop-sequence behavior -> affects billing and model outputs. Need mapping rules and example conversions.
SE feedback (Priya): recommend running the Redwood Optimize profile during POC to capture batching and KV caching gains. Also instrument Console per-route dashboards for prompt set regressions.

Quoted from AE call: "We can't lose our chat latency — customer experience drops and retention impact is measurable." Also: "Pricing needs to beat current vendor by 20% or strong SLA/uptime guarantee."

Regression risks called out: subtle output shifts on NER/summarization after quantized variants tested; also embedding drift when switching tokenizer/normalization. Plan to run Golden Prompt set (5k prompts) and automated eval harness during POC.

Security/compliance: require SSO (SAML), SOC2 + audit logging, KMS integration for key control, and option for data residency in us-west-2. Procurement will escalate dedicated VPC checklist to InfoSec.

Migration plan (high level): 1) Hosted POC with openai-compat -> measure parity and cost; 2) If parity met, negotiate Dedicated capacity (regional pools) with canary routing; 3) Gradual workspace migration with routing policy + automatic fallback to legacy vendor for regressions; 4) Full cutover after two-week canary with rollback window.

Tech details to validate: streaming SSE semantics, function-calling JSON schema parity, token counting for cost modeling, embedding dimension match and indexing pipeline (Annoy/FAISS parity), model selection/quantization recommendations for latency targets.

Commercial touchpoints: pricing deck shared (drive:/decks/prismbridge-redwood-pricing-v2.pdf). AE to deliver Dedicated proposal with commit tiers (3/6/12 months) and SLAs. Finance wants clear unit economics and burn-down curves.

Next actions captured: set up hosted API keys with usage cap, deploy sample retrieval index, run baseline evals (ff_2026-02-18_8462 transcript), schedule dedicated pricing review w/ sales on 2026-03-10.

Internal notes: PrismBridge has strict change freeze windows around end-of-quarter; prefer cutover before 2026-08 or after 2026-09 window. Keep CSM looped early (Luis Ortega) for migration success metrics and onboarding.

Potential upsell: Redwood Optimize & longer retention observability add-on to track quality regressions over time. PrismBridge open to buying eval-run credits for a 6-week deep regression suite if initial POC is positive.
